messages:
lina: Heads-up — we need to provision GPU capacity in me-central1 for a new client (low-latency embeddings + periodic batch trains). Proposal: two nodepools
- embed-compact: 1x compact GPU (T4 or a2-highgpu-1g), min=2 max=6, autoscaler tuned for latency-sensitive requests
- train-burst: mix of preemptible high-memory GPUs (prefer A100/H100 if available, fallback to a10g), min=0 max=40, scale-down aggressive to save cost
Any regional quota or IP limitations we should preflight before raising requests? Also need NAT egress and secondary IP ranges for pods. Prefers preemptible for train-burst. TL;DR: size suggestions + quota checklist?

cheng: +1 to two-pool approach. Quick checklist:
- check GPU quota (GPUs & vCPU) for me-central1
- check regional SKU availability (H100/A100 often limited)
- reserve NAT gateway IPs (we hit ephemeral shortage last quarter)
- ensure pod IP secondary ranges are big enough (maxPods calc)
If H100 quota is uncertain, recommend a10g fallback for training in this region.

zach: also watch maxPods per node — default can cause podIP exhaustion if we run many sidecars. If using 1 GPU/node, set --max-pods=64 or use ip-alias / bigger secondary range. We had a cluster in ap-south where pod IPs ran out quickly.

ana: can we get rough workload numbers? guesstimate GPU-hours / month and peak concurrent requests for embedding. will do cost estimate.

lina: peak embedding RPS ~200 qps, avg request size small, want p99 < 50ms. training jobs ~8–12 hours each, 3–5 jobs/week, usually 8 GPUs/job when available. rough monthly GPU hours ~1500–2500.

oliver: for embed-compact, prefer dedicated compact nodes (T4 / A2) pinned to low latency routing and enable nodeLocalCache for model artifacts. that can reduce GPU memory thrash and startup latency. also think about prefix caching + KV cache on runtime.

cheng: example gcloud create command skeleton (GKE Autopilot not used):
```
gcloud container node-pools create embed-compact --cluster=redwood-me --machine-type=a2-highgpu-1g --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-t4,count=1 --num-nodes=2 --enable-autoscaling --min-nodes=2 --max-nodes=6 --node-taints=inference=embed:NoSchedule --metadata=disable-legacy-endpoints=true
```
For train-burst we want preemptible + mixed instance types; set autoscaler policies with scaleDownUnneededTime=5m.

kube-bot: reminder: cluster-autoscaler version must support multiple node group balancing and mixed-instance policies. Current cluster at v1.27.3 has known bug with scale-to-zero + taints — recommend patch v1.27.5.

zach: networking note: request /23 for pod secondary range (or at least /24 with large max-pods tweak). NAT egress: reserve 3 static IPs for initial rollout (can add later, but provisioning lead time is ~48h in region).

ana: cost sketch: if we use A10G fallback for training and T4 for embed: monthly ~= $Xk (will post exact once quotas confirmed). preemptible saves ~60% for training hours.

lina: action items:
- @cheng to verify SKU availability & start quota requests for GPUs + vCPU (I will provide billing account)
- @zach to confirm pod secondary range and NAT IP availability, open infra ticket if /23 needed
- @ana to post cost estimate once quotas known
- @oliver/eng-runtime to advise on nodeLocalCache + model artifact placement
Anyone object to me opening the quota request today? :point_up:

cheng: No objections, go ahead. I'll cc infra-ops on the quota ticket and add fallback SKUs.

deploy-bot: deploy job queued: infra/quota-checker v2 -> running checks against me-central1 (ETA 6m).
